title: QuantumFlux \u0014 Discovery: migration OpenAI -> Dedicated
summary: Initial discovery for migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated. Customer focused on eval parity, latency, cost, and private deployment options (VPC/KMS). SE discussed compatibility, vLLM/TGI runtime concerns, KV cache and batching tradeoffs. Next steps: share pricing, security pack, and run a small benchmark using their prompt set.

Diego: share compatibility doc for vLLM/TGI and model conversion notes (2026-03-06)

Schedule 1hr benchmark run with Redwood SEs week of 3/9

transcript:
Header:
2026-03-04 15:00 UTC  Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Park (QuantumFlux Head of ML), Omar Singh (QuantumFlux CTO), Priya Patel (QuantumFlux ML Eng)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time, quick intro, i'm maya from redwood, and with me is diego our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Lena Park: hi, lena here, thanks  excited to talk through migration, we've been on openai for inference but running into cost and latency spikes.
[00:16] Omar Singh: yes hi, omar  want to see if dedicated infra buys us predictability, also need strong security controls.
[00:24] Diego Alvarez: great, we hear that a lot. quick agenda  current stack, workloads, eval parity, security requirements, and next steps for a pilot. sound good?
[00:32] Priya Patel: yeah, that's perfect.
[00:36] Lena: so our stack  prod uses OpenAI gpt-4 for chat features, some TGI/vLLM experiments in-house for lower latency inference on trimmed models. we call openai via server-side, about 12 million tokens/month, peak qps around 60. latency target is sub-350ms 95th for assistant responses; right now we're seeing 400-800ms depending on prompt.
[00:56] Maya: thanks. and on the vLLM/TGI side  are those self-hosted in k8s or on dedicated instances?
[01:02] Priya: self-hosted k8s cluster, using vLLM for some reranking and lightweight assistants. we tried TGI but ran into memory fragmentation and slower throughput.
[01:10] Diego: ok that aligns with what we see in the field  vLLM can be great but has tuning knobs; TGI often needs kernel-level tuning. with redwood dedicated we provide an opinionated serving runtime that handles batching, KV cache management, and kernel selection to avoid a lot of that ops work.
[01:27] Omar: two main questions  1) can you match our eval parity vs OpenAI outputs? and 2) can you meet our latency SLOs without blowing the cost?
[01:36] Maya: both great points. diego, want to talk parity and tuning?
[01:40] Diego: sure. eval parity comes down to model selection, tokenization parity, and prompt engineering. we have a model catalog with verified profiles; for many teams we recommend pinned model variants that match OpenAI-like behavior, and we can run an eval harness to measure metrics side-by-side. 
[01:56] Lena: when you say model catalog  are those open weights we host, or are you translating oracle calls to openai?
[02:03] Diego: we host open models (and can run certain licensed weights) on the Dedicated cluster. we do not proxy OpenAI; instead customers pick a model that meets their quality bar. part of the pilot is to run your prompt set against a few candidate models to measure BLEU/ROUGE/ MRR and human eval parity.
[02:20] Priya: we care a lot about tokenization differences  small whitespace differences can change outputs. will you run tokenization parity checks?
[02:27] Diego: yes, we include tokenization and temperature/seed controls in the harness. we also capture diffs and examples for manual review.
[02:34] Omar: on security  we need VPC, KMS integration, SAML SSO, audit logs, and SOC2. can Dedicated run in our VPC or do you host?
[02:44] Maya: two deployment modes  Redwood Dedicated can be in a customer VPC with private networking and customer-managed KMS for keys. we also offer Private for on-prem. SOC2 and enterprise audit logs are part of the enterprise pack; we'll send the SOC2 pack and network architecture diagram.
[02:58] Priya: good. what about data residency and retention policies? we need 90-day retention for logs, and the user data must not leave region.
[03:06] Diego: retention policies are configurable and logs can be stored in your cloud account. we'll note that for the pilot  region pinning is supported.
[03:12] Lena: back to runtime  you mentioned KV cache, batching. our workload has many short-turn conversations with long context reuse; caching prefix keys would help reduce tokens and latency. how does redwood's KV cache work?
[03:25] Diego: we do prefix and KV cache management automatically; the runtime can keep warm KV caches across requests for the same session, and we do continuous batching with the goal of improving throughput without spiking tail latency. there are knobs to prioritize latency vs total throughput.
[03:40] Omar: what's the fallback if a model fails or capacity is saturated? we can't have user-facing errors.
[03:45] Maya: we offer routing policies and automatic fallback to cheaper/compatible variants, and health-based routing across regions or tiers. SEs can set canary rollouts and automatic rollback.
[03:55] Priya: about the vLLM/TGI compatibility  we have some homegrown operators and custom kernels; will moving to redwood force us to rewrite inference code?
[04:03] Diego: usually no. Redwood provides a runtime with a compatible API layer; you can bring your own model weights as long as they follow expected model formats (ONNX/pt/gguf for quantized). we also provide conversion docs; for vLLM-specific optimizations we can share a compatibility checklist.
[04:18] Lena: cost question: right now OpenAI bill is unpredictable. how do you estimate cost and what levers do you provide?
[04:25] Maya: Dedicated is usage + reserved capacity model  you get predictable baseline capacity and lower per-token costs. Optimize provides batching, quantization recommendations, and caching suggestions to cut unit cost. we'll share a sample TCO calculator.
[04:36] Omar: any customer examples of moving from OpenAI to dedicated and keeping parity?
[04:41] Maya: yes, several case studies  we'll include reference contacts and a short deck. one customer did a three-week pilot, ran a side-by-side eval, and kept 98% parity by retuning prompts and selecting a slightly larger open model.
[04:56] Priya: what about long-term model updates  if we retrain or fine-tune, how does rollout work?
[05:02] Diego: rollout supports canary and A/B, automatic fallback and model pinning per route. we also integrate with CI to automate model pushes with pre-deploy eval gates.
[05:12] Lena: network egress  if Dedicated is in your managed infra is there egress for logging? we need to centralize logs to our SIEM.
[05:19] Maya: logs can be shipped to your cloud storage or SIEM via secure connectors; we can set up private peering.
[05:24] Omar: latency numbers  can you meet 350ms 95th for our prompts?
[05:29] Diego: likely yes for many model choices; depends on sequence length and model size. as a rule, quantized int8 models with warming and KV cache often meet those latencies at modest QPS. we'll validate with your traces in the benchmark run.
[05:42] Priya: any concerns about hallucination differences vs OpenAI? sometimes outputs are less grounded in open models.
[05:49] Diego: that's a known tradeoff. we recommend instruction-tuned variants and guardrails in the prompt layer; Redwood Optimize can run quality monitors and regression alerts tied to your eval sets.
[06:00] Lena: timeline  we want to decide by end of Q2 and start a pilot in April. is that realistic?
[06:06] Maya: yes, a pilot in April is reasonable. next immediate steps: we'll send pricing, security docs, compatibility notes, and propose a benchmark window.
[06:16] Omar: ok great. anything else we should be aware of?
[06:20] Diego: just one more note  if you plan to bring large private models or fine-tuned checkpoints, we recommend discussing quantization options early; they materially change throughput and memory footprint.
[06:30] Priya: makes sense.
[06:33] Maya: recap of action items and we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark. thanks everyone.
[06:40] Lena: thanks, bye.

Notes: some timestamps approximate; occasional transcription errors (e.g., 't g i' vs TGI). References shared: security pack link (sent after call), pricing spreadsheet (to be sent).
